source.snippet: I just had a talk with one of my first ongoing clients... He is one of those people who has a broad understanding of the tech out there... He wanted to show me, and get my opinion on a restaurant management app that he's been using Lovable to develop... [implying the output needed professional review and fix-up]

problem_statement: Small business owners using AI no-code builders (Lovable, Bolt, etc.) to develop real business applications end up with broken or incomplete apps and no way to validate or fix them without hiring a developer — creating an unmet demand for lightweight QA and remediation services for vibe-coded business apps.
target_segment: SMB owners (restaurant, retail, services) who have used AI app builders to create internal tools and need professional review, debugging, or handoff to production-quality code.
notes: Client was actively paying for Lovable (a paid subscription product) and had built a meaningful restaurant management app — clear buyer who has already spent money on the problem. The freelancer was being consulted for professional judgment, suggesting willingness to pay for QA or handoff services. Signal is a single anecdote but the pattern (paid AI builder → quality gap → developer rescue) is plausible at scale. Buyer: SMB owner already spending on AI tooling.
